Absolute must first infer the likely question domain, then determine whether a stable reading exists, identify the strongest hidden-state hypothesis, search for a false premise, generate the strongest competing explanation, calculate its own uncertainty, and refuse any detail that is not actually supported.

Three visible people appear involved, but determine whether an unmentioned fourth actor is actually controlling the matter.
The client asks whether an event will happen. Determine whether the strongest indication suggests it has already happened but has not yet become known to the client.
Can two apparently contradictory claims both be true because they refer to different stages, locations, or actors?
The visible obstacle is money. Determine what is causing the money problem itself.
Person A distrusts Person B because B delays. B delays because A distrusts him. Identify whether the case contains a self-reinforcing loop rather than a single root cause.
One testimony strongly supports the client’s theory, but the full chart opposes it. Determine whether the local indicator is valid but misleading in the broader case.
The matter appears favorable only if another event occurs first. Identify the prerequisite event and whether it is itself likely.
A person may be telling the truth about one fact while deliberately using that truth to hide a more important fact. Detect both layers.

Person A appears to be dealing directly with Person B. Determine whether an unseen intermediary is actually shaping the exchange.
Is the intermediary accurately relaying information, selectively editing it, delaying it, or manipulating both parties?

Is the claimed shortage real, temporarily inaccessible, deliberately concealed, or being used as an excuse?

Is the client being deceived by another person, or mainly deceiving themselves through wishful interpretation?
The client has repeated the same suspicion so strongly that it may bias interpretation. Perform a blind reconstruction and compare it against the client-led reading.
Strip all adjectives, accusations, emotions, and conclusions from the client’s story. Rebuild the case using only events and relationships.
